lots.title: Building Services Specification – Reactive Works (Lot 9): Provision of Reactive Repairs to Corporate Buildings
lots.description: Draft specification for Lot 9 of the London Borough of Bexley 6278 Building Services Framework, covering the delivery of reactive maintenance across the Council's Corporate estate. The Supplier is responsible for the safe, compliant, and efficient operation of all mechanical, electrical, building fabric, and specialist facilities management assets, including 24/7 emergency cover, reactive repairs to M&E, fabric, and life-safety systems, fault investigations and root-cause analysis, make-safe actions, and follow-on works. The contract commences in September 2026 and requires integration with the Council's CAFM system (Civica / TF Cloud).
requirements: Achieve and maintain statutory compliance across all assets.
Support business continuity through proactive maintenance and rapid response to failures.
Optimise asset lifecycle performance and reduce whole-life costs.
Deliver services in accordance with industry best practice, including SFG20, CIBSE Guide M, and manufacturer recommendations.
Provide accurate and timely data management through integration with the Council's CAFM system (Civica / TF Cloud).
Adopt a risk-based, proactive approach ensuring reliability, safety, and sustainability throughout the contract term.
Provide 24/7 emergency cover and a 24/7 helpdesk and emergency response capability for all critical systems, including BMS alarms, life safety systems, and essential plant.
Deliver reactive repairs to all M&E, fabric, and life-safety systems, fault investigations and root cause analysis, make-safe actions, and follow-on works as required.
Perform comprehensive asset verification, tagging, and onboarding (Mobilisation and Asset Collection) into the Council's CAFM system.
Deliver sustainability initiatives and measurable social value outcomes in line with Council objectives.

Full compliance with Health and Safety at Work, Fire Safety Act 2021, CDM 2015, Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012, PUWER, LOLER, PSSR, HSE Approved Code of Practice L8 (Legionella control), relevant BS EN standards, CIBSE Guide M, and SFG20.
Maintain current, accurate, audit-ready documentation and certifications at all times during the contract term.

Adhere to Service Level Agreements with the following response and resolution times: Priority 1 Emergency – Response 2 hours / Resolution 24 hours (make safe); Priority 2 Urgent – Response 1 working day / Resolution 2 working days; Priority 3 Standard – Response 2 working days / Resolution 4 working days; Priority 4 Non-Urgent – As agreed. All delays must be escalated immediately with mitigation proposals.
All reactive works must be carried out by appropriately certified and competent engineers, with manufacturer accreditations where applicable.
Investigate and report on the root cause of failures, implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
Upload all reactive maintenance activities, including fault reports, remedial actions, and associated certification, to the Council's CAFM system (Civica / TF Cloud) within 48 hours of completion.
Align all remedial maintenance with the planned maintenance regime to minimise downtime and optimise asset performance.
Prepare and submit site-specific Risk Assessment and Method Statements (RAMS) for all works.
Conduct dynamic risk assessments to address changing site conditions.
Comply with Council Health & Safety policies and procedures.
Perform asbestos register checks prior to commencing any work and invoke immediate stop-work procedures if Asbestos Containing Materials (ACM) are encountered.
Adhere strictly to permit-to-work systems for hot works, electrical isolations, confined spaces, and roof access.
Ensure all operatives are trained, competent, and equipped to work safely, with documentation maintained and available for audit.
Operate an ISO 14001-compliant Environmental Management System and demonstrate sustainable practices throughout the contract.
Segregate waste streams and arrange legal disposal via approved and licensed waste carriers.
Implement carbon reduction measures and energy efficiency optimisations during maintenance and operational activities.
Provide recommendations for low-carbon asset replacements and environmentally responsible alternatives.
Commit to local employment, apprenticeships and work placements, SME engagement within the supply chain, and sustainability initiatives.

Provide a comprehensive mobilisation plan within 10 working days of contract award, with a mobilisation period of typically 6–12 weeks (elsewhere stated 6–8 weeks) covering competency matrix and staffing plan, and full system integration / onboarding with the Council CAFM (TF Cloud) including data migration and validation.
Accurately record and upload all verified asset data to the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud) within the agreed timeframe, providing a comprehensive report detailing findings and any identified gaps.

Produce monthly operational reports including PPM completion, reactive performance, statutory compliance tracker, risk register, social value tracker, energy-saving opportunities, performance dashboard, exception reporting, continuous improvement actions, financial summary, and forward look, submitted electronically and presented at monthly contract review meetings.

evidence_anchors.anchor_text: London Borough of Bexley — Building Services Specification — Reactive Works — Contract Commencement SEPT 2026
This specification sets out the requirements for the delivery of Reactive Maintenance across the Corporate estate.
24/7 emergency cover; Reactive repairs to all M&E, fabric, and life-safety systems; Fault investigations and root cause analysis; Make-safe actions; Follow-on works as required.
Health and Safety at Work; Fire Safety Act 2021; CDM 2015; Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012; PUWER; LOLER; PSSR; HSE Approved Code of Practice L8; Relevant BS EN standards; CIBSE Guide M; SFG20.

Priority 1 Emergency – Response 2 hours / Resolution 24 hours (make safe); Priority 2 Urgent – Response 1 working day / Resolution 2 working days; Priority 3 Standard – Response 2 working days / Resolution 4 working days; Priority 4 Non-Urgent – As agreed.
Strict adherence to permit-to-work systems for: Hot works; Electrical isolations; Confined spaces; Roof access.
Full onboarding and integration with the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud), is mandatory, including data migration and validation.
All verified asset data must be accurately recorded and uploaded to the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud) within the agreed timeframe.
Core KPIs: 95% PPM completion monthly; 90–95% reactive response compliance; 80% first‑time fix rate; Data upload within 48 hours; Zero major H&S breaches; Quarterly social value delivery.
Monthly operational reports including PPM completion, reactive performance, statutory compliance tracker, risk register, social value tracker, and energy-saving opportunities.
